domain_label: Question Craft & Answering — Item-Writing Science & Bank Metadata (NBME/JCNDE-grounded)
purpose: A method for the study system to WRITE defensible one-best-answer test items — applying the NBME item-writing canon (cover-the-options, focused vignette, homogeneous distractors, no negative lead-ins, application over recall), tagging each item with its Bloom level and blueprint metadata, and calibrating it with classical (p-value, point-biserial, discrimination index) and IRT (1PL/2PL/3PL) psychometrics — while never inventing an exam statistic or blueprint enumeration the research file did not verify.
assumptions: no observed exam item bank or examinee response matrix is supplied; every base score is a heuristic prior, and every p-value/r_pb/discrimination band cited is a published FACT range used as an authoring TARGET, not this bank's measured statistic

the NBME Item-Writing Guide, JCNDE INBDE guides and ETS pages were verified this session via search-engine excerpts quoting the named official page (the sandbox egress proxy returned 403 for nbme.org, jcnde.ada.org and ets.org), never by reading the PDF body; the ~13 flaw-category count is an [ESTIMATE] from a secondary summary
this KB is the writing/metadata layer; the per-exam format typology and per-format answering strategy live in the sibling KB kb_item_typology and are not re-derived here

Bloom's revised taxonomy (remember/understand/apply/analyze/evaluate/create; Anderson and Krathwohl 2001) and the CTT/IRT definitions are treated as FACT with cited sources, applied as bank-design priors
exclusions: the per-exam question-format enumeration (INBDE standalone/itemset/case; TOEFL task types) and the per-format answering/directive-learning strategy — those belong to the sibling KB kb_item_typology
exam scoring and scaling mechanics (e.g. the INBDE 49-99 scaled score) beyond naming that JCNDE weighs difficulty, discrimination and guessing (a 3PL-style intent)
authoring the actual dental or English subject-matter content of any item; this KB governs item FORM, flaw-avoidance and metadata, not clinical or linguistic truth
the scheduler/adaptive-theta specialist that consumes irt_b to match item difficulty to learner ability; this KB emits the b parameter but does not own the matching
inventing the INBDE clinical-content-item enumeration, any pass rate, fee, or exam statistic the research file did not verify

competency_questions.question: What is the one-best-answer format the system should default to, and how many options should an item carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ONE_BEST_ANSWER_FORMAT states that options must be rankable on a single dimension with exactly one defensibly best option, cites the INBDE fact that all items are one-best-answer with 3-5 choices, and names it the dominant NBME format

competency_questions.question: How does the cover-the-options rule test whether a lead-in is focused?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVER_THE_OPTIONS_RULE states that a focused lead-in lets the reader cover the options and produce the answer unaided, and that failing it means the lead-in is unfocused or the item is a true/false set in disguise

competency_questions.question: How should a clinical vignette stem be structured, and what is the Patient Box?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VIGNETTE_STEM_STRUCTURE gives the canonical clinical order (age/sex/site -> chief complaint -> history -> exam -> labs/imaging) then a focused lead-in with no red-herring padding, and names the INBDE Patient Box as that idea made into a fixed template

competency_questions.question: What makes options homogeneous and distractors plausible without leaking cues?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOMOGENEOUS_OPTIONS requires all options grammatically parallel, same category and judged true/false on one dimension, and PLAUSIBLE_DISTRACTOR_DESIGN builds distractors from common errors homogeneous with the key and attractive to the non-master

competency_questions.question: Why should negatively phrased lead-ins be avoided, and what is the rewrite move?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AVOID_NEGATIVE_LEADIN states that EXCEPT/NOT lead-ins measure reading care over knowledge and gives the mental rewrite (mark each option true/false, pick the false one) plus the preferred positive one-best rewrite

competency_questions.question: What are the two families of technical item flaws, and what are their signature examples?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IRRELEVANT_DIFFICULTY_FLAWS lists long/complex options, vague frequency terms, nonparallel options, unordered numerics and none/all-of-the-above, and TESTWISENESS_CUES lists grammatical cues, absolute terms marking wrong options, the longest/most-detailed key, word repeats and convergence cues, noting the ~13 flaw categories as an estimate

competency_questions.question: Why does NBME push application over recall, and how does item format bound the Bloom level?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: APPLICATION_NOT_RECALL states NBME prefers vignette-based decision items (diagnosis, next step) over which-is-true recall, and BLOOM_LEVEL_TAGGING states MC most easily assesses remember/understand, vignette framing pushes apply/analyze, and create is out of reach for single-answer MC

competency_questions.question: What Bloom mix should a board-style bank target?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BANK_BLOOM_MIX prescribes a mostly apply/analyze bank with remember-level items reserved as terminology gates early in the learning ladder, flagged as a standard-practice estimate

competency_questions.question: What metadata should the bank record per item, and how is the INBDE blueprint handled honestly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BLUEPRINT_CONTENT_TAGS names the INBDE two-axis Foundation-Knowledge x Clinical-Content blueprint and holds the exact clinical-content-item enumeration [UNKNOWN] pending official-PDF access, and ITEM_METADATA_SCHEMA lists the minimum per-item tag set (exam, blueprint axes, format, bloom_level, stimulus, learning_objective_id, source_ref)

competency_questions.question: What are the classical difficulty and discrimination statistics and their working bands?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIFFICULTY_P_VALUE gives p = proportion correct (0-1; 0.30-0.70 for discriminating items, 0.80-1.00 for mastery), POINT_BISERIAL_DISCRIMINATION gives r_pb >=0.20 acceptable / >=0.30 good / ~0.40+ excellent / <0.20 poor / negative = miskey, and DISCRIMINATION_INDEX_D gives D = p(upper 27%) - p(lower 27%) with its bands

competency_questions.question: Why must difficulty and discrimination be read together, and what does distractor analysis check?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIFFICULTY_DISCRIMINATION_COUPLING states discrimination is maximal near mid-difficulty and shrinks as p->0 or 1, and DISTRACTOR_ANALYSIS requires every distractor be chosen by >~5% of takers and correlate negatively with total score, flagging a never-chosen distractor as dead weight

competency_questions.question: What are the IRT models in one line each, and what should the bank store and feed downstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IRT_PARAMETER_MODELS gives 1PL/Rasch (difficulty b only), 2PL (adds discrimination a), 3PL (adds guessing asymptote c) as a logistic function of ability theta, and IRT_BANK_INTEGRATION stores p_value/r_pb/n_exposures/irt_b(+a,c)/last_calibrated, quarantines r_pb<0 or dead distractors, and feeds irt_b to the scheduler

competency_questions.question: What is the end-to-end write-and-review gate that decides whether an item ships?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ITEM_WRITE_REVIEW_GATE composes the checks: cover-the-options passes, options homogeneous and flaw-free of both families, no negative lead-in, correct Bloom and complete metadata, and (post-exposure) non-negative r_pb with no dead distractor, conditioning ship on every check clearing

glossary.definition: The dominant NBME/INBDE item format: a stem plus 3-5 options rankable on a single dimension where exactly one option is the defensibly best answer and the rest are plausible but inferior; distinct from true/false or multiple-response formats. [FACT - INBDE items are exclusively one-best-answer with 3-5 choices, JCNDE Candidate Guide via excerpt]

The focus test for a lead-in: a properly focused lead-in lets a competent test-taker read the vignette and lead-in, cover the options, and produce the answer unaided; if they cannot, the lead-in is unfocused or the item is a true/false set in disguise. [FACT - NBME Item-Writing Guide via excerpt]

The final line of the stem that poses the actual question (e.g. 'Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?'); it must be focused enough to satisfy the cover-the-options rule and should be positively phrased.

The clinical stem presenting patient data in canonical order (age/sex/site -> chief complaint -> history -> exam -> labs/imaging) with all data the decision needs and no red-herring padding; the INBDE Patient Box is that idea made into a fixed standardized patient-summary template. [Patient Box FACT; canonical order ESTIMATE-high]

Options that are grammatically parallel, drawn from the same category, and judged true/false on one dimension so distractors are directly related to the lead-in and homogeneous with the key — plausible to the non-master. [FACT - NBME guide via excerpt]

A wrong option; a good distractor encodes a common examinee error, is homogeneous with the key, and is chosen by >~5% of takers with a negative correlation to total score. A never-chosen distractor is dead weight that functionally reduces the option count. [>5% and dead-distractor = ESTIMATE, standard item-analysis practice]

The two families of technical flaw: irrelevant difficulty confuses everyone (long/complex options, vague frequency terms, nonparallel or unordered options, none/all-of-the-above), while testwiseness cues help the savvy (grammatical cues, absolute terms marking wrong options, the longest/most-detailed key, word repeats, convergence cues). The guide catalogs ~13 categories. [families FACT; count ESTIMATE]

The cognitive process an item demands on the Anderson-Krathwohl 2001 scale (remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create); MC most easily assesses remember/understand, vignette framing pushes apply/analyze, and create is out of reach for single-answer MC. [FACT - taxonomy; PMC9727608 on format bounding level]

The proportion of examinees answering an item correctly (0-1; higher = easier); working ranges are 0.30-0.70 for discriminating items and 0.80-1.00 acceptable for mastery items. [FACT - Arizona item-analysis, assess.com]

The correlation between the 0/1 item score and total test score; >=0.20 acceptable, >=0.30 good, ~0.40+ excellent, <0.20 poor, and a negative r_pb flags a miskeyed or defective item. [FACT - Arizona/assess.com/cogn-iq]

p(upper 27% group) - p(lower 27% group); published medical-education bands: <=0.20 poor, 0.21-0.24 acceptable, 0.25-0.34 good, >=0.35 excellent; maximal near mid-difficulty. [FACT - PMC12805726, cogn-iq]

Item Response Theory models the probability of a correct response as a logistic function of latent ability theta: 1PL/Rasch uses difficulty b only (b = theta at P=0.50), 2PL adds discrimination a (slope), 3PL adds a guessing asymptote c (floor for low theta). JCNDE's scaled scoring weighs difficulty, discrimination and guessing — a 3PL-style intent. [FACT - cogn-iq/assess.com/PMC5875705; JCNDE FAQ via excerpt]

nodes.definition: Fix the default item format the system writes to: one-best-answer (Type A). The options must be rankable on a single dimension with exactly one defensibly best option; the rest are plausible but inferior, not simply false. All INBDE items are one-best-answer with 3-5 answer choices, and the NBME guide names this the dominant format [FACT - JCNDE Candidate Guide and NBME Item-Writing Guide via search excerpts; PDFs 403 this session]. Searches surfaced no multiple-response, ordering, drag-and-drop or hotspot formats on the INBDE, so the system does not author them for that exam. The single-dimension rankability constraint is what makes every downstream flaw check (homogeneity, cover-the-options) well-defined.

included: the exclusion of multiple-response/ordering/hotspot for the INBDE
excluded: the answering strategy for solving items

pros.claim: Committing to one-best-answer makes homogeneity and the cover-the-options test well-defined instead of ambiguous
pros.example: requiring 'the most likely diagnosis' among 5 ranked options rather than a select-all set with no single key

cons.claim: One-best-answer cannot assess create-level cognition and forces genuinely multi-answer clinical situations into a single-key mold
cons.example: a management scenario with several defensible next steps squeezed into one artificial best answer

failure_modes: writing a true/false set disguised as a multiple-choice item
authoring a format (multiple-response, ordering) the target exam does not use
acceptance_tests: the item presents 3-5 options rankable on one dimension with exactly one defensibly best option, and no unsupported format is used for the INBDE
revisit_triggers: an official guide update introduces or confirms a new item format
the target exam changes (e.g. a TOEFL productive task) so the format default no longer applies
a pretest pilots a non-standard format

base.update_signal: an official item-format update or a target-exam change revises the default format

nodes.definition: Structure the stem as a clinical vignette in canonical order: age/sex/site -> chief complaint -> history -> examination -> labs/imaging, then a focused lead-in. The stem must contain every datum the decision needs and no red-herring padding [ESTIMATE - high confidence; canonical NBME teaching, exact wording unverified this session]. The INBDE Patient Box is exactly this idea made into a fixed standardized patient-summary table (demographics, chief complaint, history, findings) that exists to enable direct skill assessment while avoiding unnecessary verbiage [FACT - INBDE Item Development Guide via excerpt]. A well-ordered vignette is what lets the lead-in be answerable with the options covered.

included: the INBDE Patient Box as a fixed template
excluded: the medical/dental truth of the clinical content
the lead-in focus test itself (its own node)

pros.claim: A canonical-order vignette with only load-bearing data lets the reader reason to the answer without hunting through padding
pros.example: a Patient Box giving age/complaint/history/findings in a fixed table the writer fills rather than free prose

cons.claim: Realistic clinical detail and irrelevant-difficulty padding look alike, so an authentic vignette can drift into noise
cons.example: adding a plausible but non-load-bearing lab value that only lengthens the stem

failure_modes: padding the stem with realistic but non-load-bearing data
scrambling the clinical order so the reader cannot scan the case
acceptance_tests: the stem follows the canonical clinical order, contains all data the lead-in needs and no red-herring padding, and uses the Patient Box template where the exam provides one
revisit_triggers: a reviewer flags padding or a missing datum in the stem
the INBDE Patient Box field set is revised
a vignette's data order confuses reviewers

base.update_signal: a padding/missing-data flag or a Patient Box field revision changes the stem structure

nodes.definition: Apply the cover-the-options rule as the primary lead-in focus test: a properly focused lead-in lets a competent reader take the vignette plus lead-in, cover the options, and produce the answer unaided [FACT - NBME Item-Writing Guide via excerpt]. If they cannot, the lead-in is unfocused (e.g. 'Which of the following is true?') or the item is really a true/false set in disguise, and the fix is to rewrite the lead-in into a single focused question — never to patch it by adding cues. This rule is the gatekeeper between a genuine one-best-answer item and a disguised true/false grid.

pros.claim: The cover-the-options test catches an unfocused lead-in before any options are written, the cheapest point to fix it
pros.example: rejecting 'Which of the following is correct regarding caries?' and rewriting to 'the most likely cause of this lesion'

cons.claim: The test is a judgment applied by the writer, so a writer who cannot answer their own focused item may wrongly blame the lead-in
cons.example: declaring a hard-but-fair lead-in unfocused because the writer lacks the content to predict the answer

failure_modes: shipping a 'which is true' lead-in that is a true/false set in disguise
patching an unfocused lead-in with grammatical or length cues instead of rewriting it
acceptance_tests: a competent reviewer can answer the item with the options covered; if not, the lead-in is rewritten into a single focused question rather than cued
revisit_triggers: reviewers repeatedly fail the cover-the-options test on an item family
a lead-in template is found to encourage 'which is true' phrasing
a disguised true/false set is discovered in the bank

base.update_signal: repeated cover-the-options failures or a disguised-true-false discovery changes the lead-in discipline

nodes.definition: Enforce option homogeneity: all options must be grammatically parallel, drawn from the same category, and judged true/false on one dimension, so that distractors are directly related to the lead-in and homogeneous with the correct answer [FACT - NBME Item-Writing Guide via excerpt]. Homogeneity is what makes distractors plausible to the non-master and simultaneously starves testwiseness cues (a heterogeneous option is the odd-one-out a savvy taker eliminates). Concretely: same option length band, same grammatical form following the lead-in, same semantic category (all diagnoses, or all next-steps, never a mix).

excluded: how distractors are sourced from common errors (its own node)

pros.claim: A homogeneous option set removes the odd-one-out cue and forces the taker to discriminate on content
pros.example: five parallel single-diagnosis options of similar length rather than one long qualified option among short ones

cons.claim: Forcing homogeneity can flatten genuinely different-category clinical choices into an artificial single category
cons.example: listing only diagnoses when the best real answer is a next-step action of a different kind

failure_modes: mixing option categories so one option is heterogeneous and eliminable
letting option length or grammar vary so the key stands out
acceptance_tests: every option is grammatically parallel, from one category, judged on one dimension, and within one length band with the key not distinguishable by form
revisit_triggers: item analysis shows takers eliminating a heterogeneous option
a category-mix is found in an option set
a length/grammar cue is flagged in review

base.update_signal: an eliminable heterogeneous option or a length/grammar cue flag changes the homogeneity rule

nodes.definition: Avoid negatively phrased lead-ins (EXCEPT / NOT): they measure reading care more than knowledge [FACT - NBME Item-Writing Guide via excerpt]. Prefer a positive one-best-answer lead-in. When a negative frame is unavoidable, the internal solving move is to rewrite it mentally as 'mark each option true/false and pick the false one' — but the writing rule is to eliminate the negative frame at authoring, not to rely on the reader's rewrite. Negative lead-ins are rare on well-built exams and common in weak banks, so the system treats an EXCEPT/NOT stem as a rewrite trigger.

included: the EXCEPT/NOT prohibition and its reading-care rationale
the true/false internal solving move as a fallback

pros.claim: Removing negative lead-ins stops an item from grading reading care instead of the target knowledge
pros.example: rewriting 'All of the following are causes EXCEPT' into 'the most likely cause is'

cons.claim: A few genuinely exclusion-shaped tasks lose precision when forced positive
cons.example: a contraindication item whose natural form is 'which is contraindicated' resisting a clean positive rewrite

failure_modes: shipping an EXCEPT/NOT lead-in that tests reading care
burying the negation mid-sentence where the reader misses it
acceptance_tests: the lead-in is positively phrased, or if a negative frame is unavoidable the negation is capitalized/emphasized and justified in review
revisit_triggers: a bank import surfaces EXCEPT/NOT items to convert
item analysis shows a negative item keying on reading not knowledge
a positive rewrite is found to distort a genuine exclusion task

base.update_signal: a negative-item import or a reading-care mis-key finding changes the negative-lead-in rule

nodes.definition: Design distractors as encoded common examinee errors that are homogeneous with the key and attractive to the non-master, so each distractor is directly related to the lead-in [FACT - NBME guide via excerpt]. A distractor should represent a mistake a partially-competent taker would actually make (a plausible wrong diagnosis, a premature next step), not an obviously absurd option. The design target is that every distractor will later earn its keep in distractor analysis (chosen by >~5% of takers, negatively correlated with total score); a distractor no one would plausibly pick is dead weight before the item is even fielded.

excluded: the empirical distractor analysis after fielding (its own node)

pros.claim: Distractors built from real common errors both discriminate and diagnose the misconception behind a wrong answer
pros.example: a distractor that is the classic look-alike diagnosis novices confuse with the key

cons.claim: Chasing maximal attractiveness can nudge a distractor toward being defensibly correct, breaking one-best-answer
cons.example: a distractor so plausible that content experts split on whether it is also acceptable

failure_modes: writing throwaway absurd distractors that no one selects
over-tuning a distractor until it becomes a second defensible answer
acceptance_tests: each distractor encodes a plausible common error, is homogeneous with the key, and is predicted to draw >~5% of takers without being defensibly correct
revisit_triggers: distractor analysis shows a distractor is dead or over-selected
a distractor is challenged as also-correct
a new common-error pattern emerges from response data

base.update_signal: a dead/over-selected distractor or an also-correct challenge changes the distractor design

nodes.definition: Purge the irrelevant-difficulty flaw family — flaws that make an item harder for everyone without testing more knowledge: long or complex options, vague frequency terms ('often', 'usually'), nonparallel options, complicated multi-part stems, numeric options not in order, and 'none of the above' / 'all of the above' [FACT - NBME guide via excerpt]. These add construct-irrelevant variance and depress discrimination. The NBME guide catalogs roughly 13 flaw categories across the two families [ESTIMATE - the exact count 13 is from a secondary summary, not the guide body]. The rule: raise difficulty through depth of reasoning, never through option or stem complexity.

included: the irrelevant-difficulty catalog (long options, vague terms, unordered numerics, none/all-of-the-above)

pros.claim: Removing irrelevant difficulty raises discrimination by cutting construct-irrelevant variance that confuses strong and weak takers alike
pros.example: ordering numeric options and deleting 'all of the above' so the item separates on knowledge

cons.claim: Some authentic complexity (a multi-value lab panel) is hard to distinguish from irrelevant difficulty
cons.example: a legitimately data-rich case reading as a complicated multi-part stem

failure_modes: leaving 'none/all of the above' or unordered numerics in the option set
buying difficulty through long or vague options instead of reasoning depth
acceptance_tests: the item is free of long/complex options, vague frequency terms, nonparallel or unordered options and none/all-of-the-above, with difficulty coming from reasoning depth
revisit_triggers: item analysis shows low discrimination traceable to an irrelevant-difficulty flaw
a new flaw pattern is added to the checklist
an NBME guide revision changes the catalog

base.update_signal: a low-discrimination flaw trace or an NBME catalog revision changes the irrelevant-difficulty checklist

nodes.definition: Purge the testwiseness-cue family — flaws that let a savvy but less-knowledgeable taker guess: grammatical cues (an option that does not follow grammatically from the lead-in), absolute terms ('always', 'never') marking an option as wrong, the longest or most-detailed option being the key, word repeats between stem and key, logical cues (a subset of options being collectively exhaustive), and convergence cues (the key sharing the most elements with other options) [FACT - NBME guide via excerpt]. These reward test-taking skill over knowledge and inflate scores for the testwise. The rule: neutralize every cue so only content distinguishes the key.

included: the testwiseness catalog (grammatical, absolute-term, longest-key, word-repeat, logical, convergence cues)
excluded: the empirical detection of cues in item analysis

pros.claim: Neutralizing cues stops the testwise from scoring above their true ability and protects item validity
pros.example: removing 'always' from a distractor and trimming the key so it is not the longest option

cons.claim: Cue-hunting can over-sanitize an item until natural language reads stilted
cons.example: awkward phrasing forced only to avoid a benign word repeat between stem and key

failure_modes: leaving the key as the longest/most-detailed option
letting an absolute term or grammatical mismatch signal the answer
acceptance_tests: no option carries a grammatical, absolute-term, length, word-repeat, logical or convergence cue that distinguishes the key from content
revisit_triggers: item analysis shows the testwise outperforming on an item
a convergence or word-repeat cue is discovered
the cue checklist is updated from a guide revision

base.update_signal: a testwise-outperformance signal or a cue-catalog revision changes the cue checklist

nodes.definition: Bias item design toward application over recall: NBME pushes vignette-based items requiring a decision (diagnosis, next step, best management) over 'which of the following is true about X' recall items [ESTIMATE - high confidence, the core stated purpose of the guide]. A recall item tests whether a fact was memorized; an application item tests whether the taker can use it on a case, which is what competence exams want. The vignette stem (with all data needed) plus a focused decision lead-in is the vehicle. Recall items are not banned — they are demoted to terminology gates (see the bank Bloom mix).

included: the application-over-recall preference and its competence rationale
the demotion of recall to terminology gates
excluded: the Bloom-level taxonomy and format bound (its own node)

pros.claim: Application items measure whether knowledge transfers to a case, the actual target of a competence exam
pros.example: asking for the next step given a vignette rather than 'which statement about the disease is true'

cons.claim: Application items are slower to write and can smuggle in construct-irrelevant reading load
cons.example: a long vignette that tests reading stamina as much as clinical reasoning

failure_modes: defaulting to 'which is true' recall items that only test memorization
writing a vignette so heavy it tests reading over reasoning
acceptance_tests: the item poses a decision on a vignette (diagnosis/next step/management) rather than a bare recall of fact, with reading load proportionate
revisit_triggers: the bank skews toward recall in a Bloom audit
an application item is found to test reading stamina
the stated exam purpose shifts toward or away from application

base.update_signal: a recall-skew audit or an exam-purpose shift changes the application-over-recall bias

nodes.definition: Tag every item with a revised-Bloom cognitive level (remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create; Anderson and Krathwohl 2001, where 'synthesis' became 'create' and moved above evaluate) [FACT - taxonomy sources]. Format bounds the level: MCQs most easily assess remember and understand, scenario/vignette framing pushes MCQs into apply and analyze, and create is effectively out of reach for single-answer MC [FACT - PMC9727608 on the taxonomy's assumption that format bounds assessable processes]. The tag is what lets the bank audit and balance its cognitive mix and is a required metadata field.

included: the format-bounds-level fact (MC reaches remember..analyze, not create)
excluded: the target bank mix across levels (its own node)

pros.claim: A Bloom tag per item makes the bank's cognitive balance auditable instead of implicit
pros.example: flagging that 80% of a section is remember-level so it can be rebalanced toward apply/analyze

cons.claim: Bloom-tagging is a judgment with fuzzy boundaries between adjacent levels
cons.example: reviewers disagreeing whether an item is understand or apply

failure_modes: mis-tagging an apply item as remember (or vice versa)
aiming an MC item at create, which the format cannot assess
acceptance_tests: each item carries one of the six revised-Bloom levels, and no single-answer MC item is tagged create
revisit_triggers: inter-rater disagreement on Bloom tags rises
the taxonomy or its bank use is revised
a new item type expands the assessable level range

base.update_signal: rising Bloom inter-rater disagreement or a taxonomy revision changes the tagging rule

nodes.definition: Target a bank-wide Bloom mix that is mostly apply/analyze (vignette plus decision), with remember-level items reserved as terminology gates early in the learning ladder, and understand items bridging between [ESTIMATE - standard board-style-bank practice, not an official quota]. The point is to match the exam's competence intent: a bank that is mostly remember-level trains recognition, not clinical reasoning, and tends to be low-discrimination. The mix is a design target the Bloom tags make auditable; it is not an NBME-published percentage, so the system states it as practice, not fact.

excluded: the discrimination statistics that recall skew depresses

pros.claim: An apply/analyze-weighted mix trains and tests reasoning and tends to discriminate better than a recall-heavy bank
pros.example: reserving remember items for a terminology-gate module and building the main bank on vignettes

cons.claim: Without an official quota the target mix is a judgment that can be set wrong for a given learner stage
cons.example: starving early learners of the remember-level gates they need before apply items

failure_modes: building a recall-heavy bank that trains recognition not reasoning
eliminating remember items entirely and stranding early learners
acceptance_tests: the bank is weighted toward apply/analyze with remember reserved for terminology gates, and the mix is stated as practice not an official quota
revisit_triggers: a Bloom audit shows the mix drifting to recall
learner outcomes suggest too few or too many terminology gates
an official blueprint publishes a cognitive-level target

base.update_signal: a Bloom-mix drift audit or an official cognitive-level target changes the bank mix

nodes.definition: Tag each item to the exam blueprint. INBDE items are classified on a two-axis blueprint: Foundation Knowledge areas x Clinical Content items [FACT - JCNDE INBDE pages via excerpts]. The exact clinical-content-item enumeration (reported as 56 clinical content items) is held [UNKNOWN] here: the official Item Development Guide and blueprint PDF were not fetchable this session (egress proxy 403 for jcnde.ada.org), and the sibling file exam_dental_us_fmg.md leaves the full enumeration pending official-PDF access. The system therefore tags the two axes it can name and never invents the missing 56-item list. Blueprint tags are what let the bank sample coverage against the exam's content map.

included: the INBDE two-axis Foundation-Knowledge x Clinical-Content blueprint
the [UNKNOWN] hold on the 56-item enumeration and its named blocker
excluded: the full per-item metadata record (its own node)

pros.claim: Blueprint tags let the bank sample and audit coverage against the exam's own content map
pros.example: reporting how many bank items map to each Foundation Knowledge area to find gaps

cons.claim: The clinical-content axis cannot be fully populated until the official enumeration is fetched, so coverage on that axis is provisional
cons.example: tagging the Foundation Knowledge axis confidently while the Clinical Content axis stays coarse

failure_modes: inventing the 56 clinical-content-item enumeration to fill a tag
leaving items untagged so coverage cannot be audited
acceptance_tests: items are tagged on the two named blueprint axes, and the clinical-content-item enumeration is held UNKNOWN with its blocker named rather than invented
revisit_triggers: the official INBDE blueprint/Item Development Guide PDF becomes fetchable
the exam publishes a revised blueprint
a coverage audit needs the finer clinical-content axis

base.update_signal: the official blueprint PDF becoming fetchable resolves the UNKNOWN clinical-content enumeration

nodes.definition: Define the minimum metadata record the bank stores per item: exam (INBDE/TOEFL), blueprint_axis1 (Foundation Knowledge), blueprint_axis2 (Clinical Content), format (standalone | itemset | case | task-type), bloom_level, stimulus (none | patient_box | image | audio), learning_objective_id, and source_ref [ESTIMATE - synthesis of exam-blueprint practice; not an official schema]. To this authoring metadata the bank later appends the psychometric fields (p_value, r_pb, n_exposures, irt_b/a/c, last_calibrated) once the item is fielded. This schema is the join key between item writing, blueprint coverage, and the scheduler that consumes difficulty.

included: the minimum authoring tag set (exam, blueprint axes, format, bloom, stimulus, LO id, source_ref)
the schema as the cross-layer join key
excluded: the values of the psychometric statistics (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A fixed minimum tag set makes every item auditable, schedulable and traceable to a source
pros.example: querying the bank for all apply-level Patient-Box items in one Foundation Knowledge area

cons.claim: The schema is a practice synthesis, not an official standard, so fields may need revision when official structures are confirmed
cons.example: renaming an axis when the official blueprint field names are finally fetched

failure_modes: admitting items to the bank without the minimum tag set
conflating authoring metadata with post-exposure statistics that do not yet exist
acceptance_tests: every item carries the full minimum tag set at authoring, with psychometric fields present but empty until the item is fielded
revisit_triggers: an official blueprint or schema publishes canonical field names
the scheduler needs a new join field
a source_ref convention change lands

base.update_signal: an official schema, a scheduler join need, or a source_ref change updates the metadata record

nodes.definition: Compute and interpret the classical difficulty index (p-value) once the item is fielded: p = the proportion of examinees answering correctly, on 0-1 where higher means easier [FACT - Arizona item-analysis, assess.com]. Working ranges: 0.30-0.70 for items meant to discriminate, and 0.80-1.00 acceptable for mastery items whose job is to confirm a floor competency. These bands are published FACT ranges used as authoring/retention TARGETS, not this bank's measured statistics (no response matrix is supplied). An item whose p sits far outside the band for its intended role (discriminating vs mastery) is a rewrite or reclassify trigger.

pros.claim: The p-value gives a single interpretable difficulty signal that flags items too easy or too hard for their role
pros.example: spotting a p=0.95 item being used where a discriminating p=0.30-0.70 item was intended

cons.claim: p is sample-dependent and says nothing about whether the item discriminates, so it must not be read alone
cons.example: a mid-p item that still fails to separate strong from weak takers

failure_modes: reading p in isolation as item quality
treating a published band as this bank's measured statistic
acceptance_tests: p is computed as proportion correct, interpreted against the 0.30-0.70 discriminating and 0.80-1.00 mastery bands, and labeled a target range not a measured value absent data
revisit_triggers: enough exposures accrue to compute a stable p
an item's p drifts outside its role band
the sample population changes so p shifts

base.update_signal: stable exposure data or a population shift changes the p-value reading

nodes.definition: Compute the point-biserial correlation (r_pb) between the 0/1 item score and the examinee's total test score as the primary discrimination statistic [FACT - Arizona/assess.com/cogn-iq]. Interpretation bands: r_pb >= 0.20 acceptable, >= 0.30 good, ~0.40+ excellent, < 0.20 poor, and a NEGATIVE r_pb flags a miskeyed or defective item where stronger takers get it wrong. r_pb is the single most actionable quality signal: a negative or near-zero value routes the item to quarantine and key-verification. As with p, these are published FACT thresholds applied as retention targets, not this bank's measured values.

included: r_pb as the primary quarantine trigger
excluded: the upper-minus-lower discrimination index D (its own node)

pros.claim: r_pb directly flags defective and miskeyed items via near-zero or negative values
pros.example: a negative r_pb revealing the answer key was set to the wrong option

cons.claim: r_pb is bounded by item difficulty, so an easy or hard item can show low r_pb despite being sound
cons.example: a legitimate mastery item at p=0.95 showing a modest r_pb by construction

failure_modes: retaining an item with negative r_pb without checking the key
judging r_pb without accounting for the item's difficulty
acceptance_tests: r_pb is computed against total score, interpreted on the >=0.20/>=0.30/0.40+ bands, and any negative r_pb triggers quarantine and key verification
revisit_triggers: r_pb crosses below 0.20 or goes negative for an item
a key correction changes an item's r_pb
the discrimination bands are updated from a source

base.update_signal: an r_pb crossing a band, a key correction, or a band update changes the discrimination reading

nodes.definition: Compute the discrimination index D = p(upper group) - p(lower group), conventionally using the upper and lower 27% of examinees by total score [FACT - PMC12805726, cogn-iq]. Published medical-education bands: D <= 0.20 poor, 0.21-0.24 acceptable, 0.25-0.34 good, >= 0.35 excellent. D is the intuitive companion to r_pb — it asks directly whether strong takers outscore weak takers on the item. Like r_pb it is bounded by difficulty and is a published-band target applied to retention, not this bank's measured value. A low or negative D corroborates an r_pb quarantine flag.

included: D as the intuitive corroborator of r_pb
excluded: the coupling of difficulty and discrimination

pros.claim: D gives a directly interpretable strong-minus-weak separation that corroborates the point-biserial flag
pros.example: a D of 0.05 confirming the r_pb-flagged item fails to separate ability groups

cons.claim: D discards middle examinees and is coarser than r_pb, so the two can disagree at the margin
cons.example: a borderline item rated acceptable by D but poor by r_pb

failure_modes: using D alone and ignoring the middle 46% of examinees
treating a published D band as this bank's measured statistic
acceptance_tests: D is computed as upper-minus-lower 27% p, interpreted on the four published bands, and read alongside r_pb rather than alone
revisit_triggers: D and r_pb disagree on an item
the upper/lower grouping fraction is changed
the D bands are updated from a source

base.update_signal: a D-vs-r_pb disagreement or a band update changes the discrimination-index reading

nodes.definition: Read difficulty and discrimination together: discrimination is mathematically maximal near mid-difficulty and shrinks toward zero as p approaches 0 or 1, so p and (r_pb, D) must never be interpreted in isolation [FACT - cogn-iq item-discrimination page via excerpt]. The consequence for item design: an item intended to discriminate should sit near mid-difficulty (p ~ 0.30-0.70), while a very high-p mastery item is expected and allowed to show modest discrimination because its job is to confirm a floor, not to separate the top. This coupling is the interpretive lens that stops the bank from culling sound mastery items for 'low discrimination'.

included: discrimination maximal at mid-difficulty, shrinking as p->0 or 1
mid-p for discriminators vs high-p allowed low-D for mastery items
excluded: the raw computation of p, r_pb and D

pros.claim: Reading the two together prevents wrongly culling sound high-p mastery items and correctly targets mid-p for discriminators
pros.example: retaining a p=0.92 floor-competency item despite a modest r_pb rather than deleting it

cons.claim: The coupling adds interpretive nuance that a naive threshold-only review can get wrong
cons.example: an automated cull rule deleting every r_pb<0.20 item including legitimate mastery gates

failure_modes: culling a legitimate mastery item for low discrimination
targeting a discriminating item at an extreme p where discrimination cannot appear
acceptance_tests: difficulty and discrimination are interpreted jointly, with mid-p targeted for discriminators and high-p mastery items retained despite modest discrimination
revisit_triggers: a cull rule is found deleting sound mastery items
the item's intended role (discriminator vs mastery) is reclassified
a source refines the coupling

base.update_signal: a mis-cull discovery or a role reclassification changes the joint difficulty-discrimination reading

nodes.definition: Run distractor analysis on fielded items: every distractor should be chosen by more than ~5% of takers and should correlate negatively with total score, while a never-chosen distractor is dead weight that functionally reduces a 4-option item to 3 [ESTIMATE - standard practice per the Arizona item-analysis page]. A distractor that the strongest takers pick, or that no one picks, is a defect to repair. This closes the loop back to plausible-distractor design: the empirical selection frequencies tell the writer which anticipated common errors were real and which distractors to replace.

excluded: the a-priori design of distractors from common errors

pros.claim: Distractor analysis pinpoints which specific options are dead or malfunctioning so the item is repaired surgically
pros.example: replacing the one distractor no taker chose while keeping the three that functioned

cons.claim: Distractor thresholds are sample- and size-dependent, so a small exposure count gives noisy per-option rates
cons.example: a distractor reading as dead only because too few takers have seen the item yet

failure_modes: leaving a dead distractor in place and reporting a 4-option item that is really 3
acting on per-distractor rates from too few exposures
acceptance_tests: each distractor is checked for >~5% selection and negative correlation with total score, and dead or positively-correlated distractors are replaced once enough exposures accrue
revisit_triggers: a distractor drops below the selection floor across a window
a distractor correlates positively with total score
exposure count reaches a stable analysis threshold

base.update_signal: a dead-distractor finding or a stable exposure threshold changes the distractor analysis

nodes.definition: State the IRT model family in one line each: IRT models the probability of a correct response as a logistic function of latent ability theta. 1PL/Rasch uses difficulty b only (b = the theta at which P(correct)=0.50, absent guessing); 2PL adds discrimination a (the slope at the inflection); 3PL adds a guessing asymptote c (the floor probability for very low theta) [FACT - cogn-iq/assess.com/PMC5875705]. JCNDE's scaled scoring explicitly weighs difficulty, how well an item distinguishes strong from weak candidates, and susceptibility to guessing — i.e. a 3PL-style parameterization [FACT - JCNDE scoring FAQ via excerpt]. b is the natural difficulty signal to feed the scheduler; a and c refine it.

excluded: the CTT statistics that approximate these parameters

pros.claim: IRT gives a sample-independent difficulty parameter b that ports across forms and drives adaptive selection
pros.example: matching an item's b to a learner's estimated theta to keep practice appropriately challenging

cons.claim: IRT calibration needs many exposures and modeling assumptions, so early or thin data cannot support 2PL/3PL fits
cons.example: attempting a 3PL fit on an item with too few exposures and getting an unstable c

failure_modes: fitting a 3PL model on insufficient exposures and reporting unstable parameters
conflating the CTT p-value with the IRT b without noting sample dependence
acceptance_tests: the three models are stated as logistic-in-theta with b, a and c defined, and the JCNDE 3PL-style scoring intent is cited as fact
revisit_triggers: exposure counts reach a level supporting 2PL or 3PL calibration
a JCNDE scoring description is revised
a model-fit diagnostic rejects the chosen parameterization

base.update_signal: sufficient exposures for calibration or a JCNDE scoring revision changes the IRT model use

nodes.definition: Integrate the statistics into the bank's calibration pipeline: store per item p_value, r_pb, n_exposures, irt_b (plus irt_a, irt_c when calibratable) and last_calibrated; recalibrate on a schedule; and quarantine items with r_pb < 0 or dead distractors [ESTIMATE - bank-implementation synthesis grounded in the FACT statistics]. IRT b is the natural difficulty signal to hand the scheduler/adaptive specialist so it can match item b to learner theta and keep practice appropriately challenging. This node is where item writing, CTT and IRT converge into a maintained, self-correcting bank rather than a static list.

included: the stored fields (p_value, r_pb, n_exposures, irt_b/a/c, last_calibrated)
scheduled recalibration and quarantine of r_pb<0 or dead-distractor items
excluded: the definitions of the individual statistics

pros.claim: A calibration pipeline turns the bank into a self-correcting asset that quarantines defects and feeds difficulty downstream
pros.example: auto-quarantining a newly-negative-r_pb item and passing every healthy item's irt_b to the scheduler

cons.claim: Calibration needs sustained exposures and a schedule, so a young bank runs on CTT approximations and provisional b values
cons.example: scheduling on p-value-derived difficulty until enough exposures allow a stable irt_b

failure_modes: running an un-analyzable bank with no stored statistics or calibration history
leaving negative-r_pb or dead-distractor items live instead of quarantining them
acceptance_tests: the bank stores the full statistic field set per item, recalibrates on schedule, quarantines r_pb<0 and dead-distractor items, and exposes irt_b to the scheduler
revisit_triggers: a recalibration cycle is due
an item newly crosses into quarantine
the scheduler changes the difficulty signal it consumes

base.update_signal: a recalibration cycle, a new quarantine, or a scheduler signal change updates the pipeline

nodes.definition: Compose the end-to-end go/no-go the whole KB builds toward: an item ships only when it clears every gate. Writing gates: one-best-answer with 3-5 options, a canonical vignette stem, a lead-in that passes cover-the-options, homogeneous options, no negative lead-in, and freedom from both the irrelevant-difficulty and testwiseness flaw families. Cognitive/metadata gates: an application-biased Bloom level correctly tagged and the full minimum metadata (blueprint axes, format, stimulus, LO id, source_ref) present. Post-exposure gates: non-negative r_pb, p within the band for the item's role read through the difficulty-discrimination coupling, and no dead distractor. Reconciled rules: never buy difficulty with a flaw; never keep a negative-r_pb or dead-distractor item; never invent the blueprint enumeration; a well-written item that fails a post-exposure statistic returns to quarantine until repaired.

included: the composed writing, cognitive/metadata and post-exposure gate set
the return-to-quarantine condition on any failed gate
excluded: the internal detail of each individual gate (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A single composed gate stops an item shipping on writing quality alone while a metadata or psychometric gate is unmet
pros.example: holding a cleanly-written item whose fielded r_pb is negative until the key is fixed

cons.claim: A single verdict can oversimplify an item whose writing is sound but whose statistics are merely provisional on thin data
cons.example: quarantining a good new item only because its early exposure count makes r_pb noisy

failure_modes: shipping on writing quality alone while a Bloom, metadata or statistic gate is unmet
treating the verdict as static when recalibration or a guide revision changes a gate
acceptance_tests: the gate conjoins the writing, cognitive/metadata and post-exposure checks, applies the reconciled flaw and quarantine rules, and returns any item failing a gate to quarantine until repaired
revisit_triggers: a recalibration flips an item's post-exposure gate
an NBME/JCNDE guide revision changes a writing gate
the blueprint enumeration becomes known and tightens the metadata gate

base.update_signal: a recalibration, a guide revision, or a resolved blueprint enumeration changes a gate in the verdict

edges.why_related: the one-best-answer format sets what the vignette stem must lead into
cover-the-options is the focus test for a one-best-answer lead-in
a well-ordered vignette is what lets the lead-in be answerable with the options covered
single-dimension rankability is what makes option homogeneity well-defined
the negative-lead-in prohibition is a specific case of keeping the lead-in focused and knowledge-testing
distractors are designed within the homogeneity constraint that keeps them parallel to the key
nonparallel and unordered options are irrelevant-difficulty flaws that homogeneity prevents
the distractors just designed are where length, absolute-term and convergence cues must be neutralized
the vignette-plus-decision stem is the vehicle for application-level items
the application-vs-recall choice determines the Bloom level the item is tagged with
per-item Bloom tags are what make the bank-wide mix auditable and targetable
the two blueprint axes are fields in the per-item metadata record
the Bloom level is a required field in the per-item metadata record
the metadata record is where the fielded p-value is stored and joined to the item
point-biserial is read against the item's difficulty which p establishes
the discrimination index D is computed from group p-values that difficulty underpins
the coupling reads discrimination against the p-value the difficulty node provides
the coupling interprets the point-biserial against difficulty
per-distractor correlations extend the item-level point-biserial down to each option
distractor analysis empirically tests which anticipated common-error distractors actually functioned
the CTT difficulty-discrimination reading motivates the IRT b and a parameters that formalize it
the model family defines the irt_b/a/c fields the calibration pipeline stores
cover-the-options is a writing gate the merged verdict composes
freedom from testwiseness cues is a writing gate the merged verdict composes
freedom from irrelevant-difficulty flaws is a writing gate the merged verdict composes
the cognitive-mix target is a gate the merged verdict composes
the post-exposure statistic and quarantine checks are gates the merged verdict composes
authentic clinical detail in a vignette and construct-irrelevant padding look alike, so richness pulls against flaw-freedom
edges.resolution_rule: include only data the lead-in's decision needs; any authentic-but-unused datum is treated as irrelevant difficulty and cut, keeping the stem focused

edges.why_related: maximizing a distractor's attractiveness can introduce length or detail cues that mark it as the odd one
edges.resolution_rule: source distractors from common errors for plausibility but equalize length, grammar and detail so no option carries a testwiseness cue

edges.why_related: cheap-to-write recall gates pull against the effortful apply/analyze items competence assessment wants
edges.resolution_rule: weight the bank toward apply/analyze vignette items and reserve remember-level items only as early terminology gates

edges.why_related: targeting an easy high-p mastery item pulls against the mid-difficulty needed for strong discrimination
edges.resolution_rule: target mid-difficulty (p 0.30-0.70) for discriminating items and accept high p with modest discrimination only for mastery gates, read through the coupling

edges.why_related: a statistically defective negative-r_pb item may be content-critical, pitting coverage against psychometric quality
edges.resolution_rule: quarantine and repair any negative-r_pb or dead-distractor item before it can ship; never retain a defective item for content coverage

edges.why_related: rich per-item statistics and repeated recalibration cost authoring and exposure effort against the value of a lean bank
edges.resolution_rule: mandate the minimum metadata tag set at authoring and defer the CTT/IRT statistic fields until enough exposures accrue to calibrate

edges.why_related: D and r_pb are two discrimination indices measuring the same strong-minus-weak separation from different math
the IRT difficulty b and the CTT p-value are two difficulty signals for the same item, one sample-independent and one sample-bound
empirical selection frequencies feed back to tell the writer which anticipated common-error distractors to keep or replace
an item that fails to discriminate feeds back to revise the stem and options that made it too easy or unfocused
leaving a testwiseness cue causally inflates the proportion correct and distorts the measured difficulty

conflict_axes.name: vignette_authenticity_vs_lead_in_focus
conflict_axes.description: A rich, authentic clinical vignette pulls against the tightly focused stem the cover-the-options rule and flaw-freedom demand, since realistic detail and construct-irrelevant padding look alike.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: include only the data the lead-in's decision needs and cut any authentic-but-unused datum as irrelevant difficulty

conflict_axes.name: difficulty_via_depth_vs_via_tricks
conflict_axes.description: Making an item hard through deeper clinical reasoning pulls against the easy path of hardness through complex options, vague terms or obscure wording.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy difficulty only through depth of reasoning; never through irrelevant-difficulty flaws that confuse strong and weak takers alike

conflict_axes.name: distractor_attractiveness_vs_cue_leakage
conflict_axes.description: Maximizing how attractive a distractor is to the non-master pulls against neutralizing the length, detail and absolute-term cues that would mark the key.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: source distractors from real common errors for plausibility but equalize length, grammar and detail so no cue survives

conflict_axes.name: one_best_answer_vs_multiple_defensible
conflict_axes.description: The one-best-answer format needs a single defensibly best option, but real clinical situations often admit several defensible answers.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rank options on one dimension and confirm with a content-expert panel that one is best; if not, rewrite the lead-in rather than ship an ambiguous key

conflict_axes.name: recall_gates_vs_application_depth
conflict_axes.description: Cheap-to-write remember-level items that gate terminology pull against the effortful apply/analyze vignette items that assess competence.
poles: fill the bank with recall gates
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight the bank toward apply/analyze and reserve remember-level items only as early terminology gates

conflict_axes.name: difficulty_target_vs_discrimination
conflict_axes.description: Very easy mastery items (high p) inherently discriminate poorly, while discriminating items must sit near mid-difficulty.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: target mid-p for discriminating items and accept high-p low-discrimination only for mastery gates, always read through the coupling

conflict_axes.name: statistical_defect_flag_vs_content_coverage
conflict_axes.description: A negative point-biserial or dead distractor flags a defective item, but that item may cover content the bank otherwise lacks.
poles: retain a defective item for coverage
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quarantine and repair any negative-r_pb or dead-distractor item before it ships; find coverage from a sound item instead

conflict_axes.name: calibration_data_vs_authoring_and_exposure_cost
conflict_axes.description: Full per-item statistics and repeated recalibration need many exposures and authoring effort against the pull of a lean, cheap-to-maintain bank.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: mandate the minimum metadata at authoring and defer CTT/IRT fields until exposures accrue, then recalibrate on a schedule

conflict_axes.name: verified_fact_vs_convenient_enumeration
conflict_axes.description: The pull to fill the INBDE clinical-content blueprint tag with an invented enumeration pulls against holding it UNKNOWN until the official PDF is fetchable.
poles: invent the blueprint enumeration to tag fully
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tag only the blueprint axes the sources name and hold the 56-item clinical-content enumeration UNKNOWN with its blocker named until the official PDF is fetched

edge_cases.description: A lead-in fails cover-the-options: the reader cannot answer with the options covered
edge_cases.trigger: a 'which of the following is true' or otherwise unfocused lead-in
edge_cases.mitigation: diagnose it as an unfocused lead-in or disguised true/false set and rewrite the lead-in into a single focused question rather than adding cues

edge_cases.description: Two options are both defensibly best, breaking the one-best-answer contract
edge_cases.trigger: a distractor tuned so plausible that content experts split on it
edge_cases.mitigation: rank on a single dimension, confirm one best option with an expert panel, and rewrite the lead-in or the distractor if two remain defensible

edge_cases.description: The longest or most-detailed option is the key
edge_cases.trigger: the correct answer is elaborated more than the distractors
edge_cases.mitigation: equalize option length and detail so the key is not distinguishable by form

edge_cases.description: An absolute term ('always', 'never') marks a distractor as wrong
edge_cases.trigger: an absolute qualifier left in a distractor
edge_cases.mitigation: remove absolute terms and phrase all options with comparable hedging so no cue distinguishes them

edge_cases.description: 'None of the above' / 'all of the above' or numeric options out of order appear
edge_cases.trigger: a lazy option set with catch-all or unordered numeric options
edge_cases.mitigation: drop none/all-of-the-above and order numeric options ascending

edge_cases.description: A negative EXCEPT/NOT lead-in ships and tests reading care over knowledge
edge_cases.mitigation: rewrite into a positive one-best-answer lead-in, or if unavoidable emphasize the negation and justify it in review

edge_cases.description: A distractor is never chosen, making a 4-option item effectively a 3-option item
edge_cases.trigger: distractor analysis shows a below-5% selection rate
edge_cases.mitigation: replace the dead distractor with a plausible common-error option once enough exposures confirm it is dead

edge_cases.description: An item shows a negative point-biserial: stronger takers get it wrong
edge_cases.trigger: item analysis returns r_pb below zero
edge_cases.mitigation: quarantine the item, verify the answer key, and rewrite the distractors or key before returning it to the bank

edge_cases.description: A very high-p mastery item is culled for low discrimination
edge_cases.trigger: a threshold-only rule deletes every r_pb<0.20 item
edge_cases.mitigation: read difficulty and discrimination jointly and retain high-p mastery gates despite modest discrimination

edge_cases.description: An item is over-exposed and its calibration and security degrade
edge_cases.trigger: n_exposures grows past a rotation threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: rotate or retire over-exposed items and recalibrate the replacements on schedule

edge_cases.description: The INBDE clinical-content enumeration is invented to fully populate a blueprint tag
edge_cases.trigger: a blueprint field is filled from memory rather than the official PDF
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the 56-item enumeration UNKNOWN with the egress-blocked official PDF named as the blocker, and tag only the axes the sources verify

edge_cases.description: A recall-heavy bank trains recognition rather than clinical reasoning
edge_cases.trigger: a Bloom audit shows the mix skewed to remember-level items
edge_cases.mitigation: shift new authoring to apply/analyze vignette items and confine remember items to terminology gates

workflow.description: Commit to one-best-answer with 3-5 single-dimension-rankable options and exclude formats the target exam does not use
workflow.gate: the item is one-best-answer with 3-5 options and no unsupported format for the exam

workflow.description: Write the stem in canonical clinical order with all decision data and no padding, using the Patient Box where provided
workflow.gate: the stem follows canonical order, carries all needed data and no red-herring padding

workflow.action: Write the lead-in and apply cover-the-options
workflow.description: Pose a single focused decision lead-in and confirm it is answerable with the options covered
workflow.gate: a reviewer can answer the item with the options covered, or the lead-in is rewritten

workflow.description: Convert any EXCEPT/NOT lead-in into a positive one-best-answer question
workflow.gate: the lead-in is positively phrased or the negation is justified and emphasized

workflow.action: Draft homogeneous options and plausible distractors
workflow.description: Build parallel same-category options with distractors from real common errors
workflow.gate: options are homogeneous and each distractor encodes a plausible common error without being defensibly correct

workflow.description: Scan for irrelevant-difficulty flaws and testwiseness cues and neutralize both
workflow.gate: the item is free of both irrelevant-difficulty flaws and testwiseness cues

workflow.action: Confirm application level and tag Bloom
workflow.description: Confirm the item poses a decision on a vignette and tag its revised-Bloom level
workflow.gate: the item is application-biased where intended and tagged one of the six levels, never create for MC

workflow.description: Populate the minimum tag set (exam, blueprint axes, format, bloom, stimulus, LO id, source_ref) with the clinical-content enumeration held UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the full minimum tag set is present and no blueprint enumeration is invented

workflow.description: Once fielded, compute p, r_pb and D and interpret them jointly through the coupling
workflow.gate: p, r_pb and D are computed and read together, with negative r_pb flagged

workflow.action: Run distractor analysis and IRT calibration
workflow.description: Check each distractor, calibrate irt_b (and a, c when possible), store the statistic fields and quarantine defects
workflow.gate: distractors are analyzed, statistics stored, defects quarantined, and irt_b exposed to the scheduler

workflow.description: Compose the writing, cognitive/metadata and post-exposure gates into a ship / quarantine verdict
workflow.gate: the item ships only when every writing, metadata and post-exposure gate clears, else it returns to quarantine

dominance_rules.rule: The cover-the-options test dominates a clever lead-in
dominance_rules.rationale: an item answerable only by reading the options is a disguised true/false set, not a one-best-answer item
dominance_rules.trigger: the reader cannot answer with the options covered
dominance_rules.action: rewrite the lead-in into a single focused question rather than patching it with cues

dominance_rules.rule: Application/vignette framing dominates recall phrasing for competence items
dominance_rules.rationale: competence exams test whether knowledge transfers to a case, not whether a fact was memorized
dominance_rules.trigger: an item is drafted as 'which of the following is true about X'
dominance_rules.action: reframe it as a decision on a vignette (diagnosis / next step) or demote it to a terminology gate

dominance_rules.rationale: difficulty bought through irrelevant-difficulty or testwiseness flaws corrupts validity rather than measuring knowledge
dominance_rules.trigger: an item is made harder via complex options, vague terms or a cue
dominance_rules.action: remove the flaw and raise difficulty only through depth of reasoning

dominance_rules.rationale: an attractive but heterogeneous or cue-leaking option is eliminable by testwiseness, defeating its purpose
dominance_rules.trigger: a distractor is made attractive by extra length, detail or a differing category
dominance_rules.action: keep options parallel, same-category and equal-length and source attractiveness from common errors

dominance_rules.rule: The negative-r_pb / dead-distractor quarantine dominates content coverage
dominance_rules.rationale: a defective or miskeyed item mismeasures ability regardless of the content it nominally covers
dominance_rules.trigger: an item shows negative point-biserial or a dead distractor
dominance_rules.action: quarantine and repair the item and source the needed coverage from a sound item

dominance_rules.rule: Mid-difficulty dominates for discriminating items; high-p is reserved for mastery gates
dominance_rules.rationale: discrimination is mathematically maximal near mid-difficulty and vanishes as p approaches 0 or 1
dominance_rules.trigger: a discriminating item is targeted at an extreme p
dominance_rules.action: target p 0.30-0.70 for discriminators and accept high-p low-discrimination only for mastery gates

dominance_rules.rule: The minimum metadata tag set at authoring dominates deferring tags
dominance_rules.rationale: an untagged item cannot be audited for coverage, balanced by Bloom, or scheduled
dominance_rules.trigger: an item is proposed for the bank without its full authoring tag set
dominance_rules.action: block admission until exam, blueprint axes, format, bloom, stimulus, LO id and source_ref are present

dominance_rules.rule: Post-exposure calibration dominates the author's a-priori difficulty guess
dominance_rules.rationale: measured r_pb and irt_b reflect real examinee behavior the author's intuition cannot
dominance_rules.trigger: an item's authored difficulty label conflicts with its fielded statistics
dominance_rules.action: trust the calibrated statistics once enough exposures accrue and relabel the item

dominance_rules.rule: The verified-source honesty label dominates any borrowed statistic or enumeration
dominance_rules.rationale: the official INBDE blueprint enumeration and any exam statistic are unverified until the official PDF is fetched
dominance_rules.trigger: a blueprint enumeration or exam statistic is about to be stated as fact
dominance_rules.action: hold it UNKNOWN with the egress blocker named, or cite the verified band as a published range, never invent it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the cover-the-options test before writing the options
anti_rework_rules.prevents: drafting a full option set for an unfocused lead-in that must be scrapped and rewritten

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the single answer dimension and confirm exactly one best option with a reviewer before drafting distractors
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a multiple-defensible-answer dispute that forces a rewrite after review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Equalize option length, grammar and parallelism at draft time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a testwiseness-cue rework pass after item review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag Bloom, blueprint, format and stimulus at authoring
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a separate re-tagging pass before the item can be audited or scheduled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reserve recall items to terminology gates from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a recall-skewed bank of low-discrimination items that must later be culled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write discriminating items to mid-difficulty, not maximal hardness
anti_rework_rules.prevents: low-discrimination items that fail item analysis and need re-authoring

anti_rework_rules.rule: Store p_value, r_pb, n_exposures and last_calibrated from the first exposure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an un-analyzable bank with no calibration history that cannot be recalibrated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every borrowed enumeration or statistic with its source and freshness before use
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented blueprint count or exam statistic propagating and later being retracted

iteration_protocol.trigger: post-exposure item analysis returns r_pb below 0.20 or negative
iteration_protocol.action: quarantine the item, verify the key, and rewrite the distractors or key before re-fielding

iteration_protocol.trigger: the official INBDE blueprint or Item Development Guide PDF becomes fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the UNKNOWN clinical-content-item enumeration with the verified list and tighten the metadata coverage audit

iteration_protocol.trigger: a distractor is chosen by fewer than ~5% of takers across an exposure window
iteration_protocol.action: replace the dead distractor with a plausible common-error option and re-verify homogeneity

iteration_protocol.trigger: an item's p-value drifts outside the band for its role (discriminating vs mastery)
iteration_protocol.action: re-target difficulty through reasoning depth, not tricks, and reclassify the item's role if warranted

iteration_protocol.trigger: enough exposures accrue to calibrate IRT for an item
iteration_protocol.action: fit irt_b (and a, c where stable), store the parameters with last_calibrated, and feed b to the scheduler

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reviewer flags a testwiseness cue or an irrelevant-difficulty flaw
iteration_protocol.action: apply the two-family flaw checklist and re-edit the stem and options

iteration_protocol.trigger: an NBME Item-Writing Guide or JCNDE guide revision changes a rule
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the flaw taxonomy and writing gates and re-audit the affected bank items

priority_rationale: The format, vignette structure and cover-the-options focus test come first because every option, flaw check and metadata tag depends on a well-formed one-best-answer stem; the homogeneity, negative-lead-in, distractor-design and two flaw-family nodes next, because they turn a stem into a defensible option set free of construct-irrelevant variance and cues; the application/Bloom and blueprint/metadata nodes then classify the item cognitively and for coverage; the p-value, point-biserial, discrimination index, their coupling, distractor analysis and IRT models next, because they are the post-exposure psychometrics that only apply once the item is fielded; and the calibration pipeline and the merged write-and-review gate come last because they compose every upstream writing, metadata and statistical check into a maintained bank and a ship / quarantine verdict.
